Latin word

hinc

adverb

from here, hence

In this lexicon

  • from here

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Haut. 211: Ego ībō hinc intrō; Mart. 13.25.1: procul hinc discēde, viātor; Traupman 319

  • Quō hinc abīs?: where are you off to?

    modern

Examples

  • Ego ībō hinc intrō, ut videam nōbīs quid cēnae siet. Tū … vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius.

    I’ll go in and see what we have for dinner. You, … mind you don’t wander too far from here.Ter. Haut. 211–212

    In the entry for from here

  • Mē ad cēnam vocā. — Pol vērō vocō. — Eāmus intrō hinc. — Fīat.

    Invite me to dinner. — I do indeed. — Let’s go in, then. — Agreed.Ter. Ph. 1053–1054

    In the entry for from here

  • pōma sumus Cybelēs: procul hinc discēde, viātor, nē cadat in miserum nostra ruīna caput

    we are Cybele’s fruit: keep well away from here, traveller, or we may fall on your poor headMart. 13.25.1–2

    In the entry for from here

  • attat! hoc illud est: hinc illae lacrimae

    aha! so that’s it: hence those tearsTer. And. 125–126
